```

shadshiny gives you surfaces and structure — cards, tabs, a sidebar shell,
resizable panes — but leaves page layout to plain CSS. This guide shows how to
assemble them into real app shells.

## Cards as the base surface

`shad_card()` is the primary container. Compose it from its parts; each is
optional:

```{r}
shad_card(
  shad_card_header(
    shad_card_title("Team members"),
    shad_card_description("Invite your colleagues to collaborate.")
  ),
  shad_card_content(
    # ... body ...
  ),
  shad_card_footer(
    shad_button("Save"), shad_button("Cancel", variant = "outline")
  )
)
```

## Container, stack, grid

Three primitives cover almost all page layout. They are CSS-only wrappers: each
argument becomes a custom property on the root, so there is no utility-class
soup and no JavaScript.

`shad_container()` is the outermost wrapper — a centred, max-width column:

```{r}
shad_container(page_content, size = "lg")   # sm/md/lg/xl/full, or a CSS length
```

`shad_stack()` is "these things, spaced" — a flex column by default, a row when
you ask:

```{r}
shad_stack(section_one, section_two, gap = 6)

shad_stack(
  shad_button("Save"), shad_button("Cancel", variant = "outline"),
  direction = "horizontal", gap = 2, align = "center"
)
```

`shad_grid()` handles two dimensions. Reach for `min_width` first — it fits as
many equal columns as will fit, with no breakpoints to reason about:

```{r}
shad_grid(card_one, card_two, card_three, min_width = "16rem")
```

When you want an exact column count, pass `cols`, optionally per breakpoint
(`base`, `sm` 40rem, `md` 48rem, `lg` 64rem). Each breakpoint falls back to the
one below it, so you only name the ones that change:

```{r}
shad_grid(a, b, c, d, cols = c(base = 1, md = 2, lg = 4))
```

`template` takes an explicit track list, and `shad_grid_item()` spans cells:

```{r}
shad_grid(
  main_panel,
  shad_grid_item(wide_chart, span = "full"),
  template = "2fr 1fr"
)
```

Gaps and padding accept a **spacing token step** — `gap = 4` is
`var(--shad-space-4)`, the same scale the components use internally — or any CSS
length when you need to escape the scale.

## Tabs

`shad_tabs()` splits a region into panes. The active pane is `input$id`; switch
it from the server with `update_shad_tabs()`.

```{r}
shad_tabs(
  "settings_tabs", selected = "profile",
  shad_tab("profile",  "Profile",  profile_ui),
  shad_tab("account",  "Account",  account_ui),
  shad_tab("billing",  "Billing",  billing_ui)
)
```

> **Outputs inside an initially-hidden tab are suspended.** A `textOutput()` or
> `plotOutput()` in a tab that isn't the `selected` one won't render until you
> switch to it — and sometimes not even then. Force it with
> `outputOptions(output, "id", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)`. The same applies to
> outputs inside a dialog or sheet that opens later.

## Page shells

Two wrappers assemble a whole page in one call. Both take the `page_shad()`
theming arguments (`theme_preset`, `dark`, `theme`) and wrap their content in a
`shad_container()` unless you pass `container = FALSE`.

`shad_page_navbar()` — a title bar carrying a tab strip, panels below. The
window scrolls; the bar is sticky. `input$<inputId>` is the active tab.

```{r}
ui <- shad_page_navbar(
  shad_tab("overview", "Overview", overview_ui),
  shad_tab("reports",  "Reports",  reports_ui),
  title = "Acme", inputId = "nav",
  header_end = bslib::input_dark_mode()
)
```

`shad_page_sidebar()` — the application frame: a collapsible sidebar, a bar with
its trigger, and a scrolling main region. This shell takes the full viewport
height and scrolls its main region rather than the window, so the sidebar rail
and footer stay put.

```{r}
ui <- shad_page_sidebar(
  sidebar = shad_sidebar(
    shad_sidebar_group("Platform",
      shad_sidebar_item("home",  "Home",  icon = "home", active = TRUE),
      shad_sidebar_item("inbox", "Inbox", icon = "mail", badge = "3"))),
  inputId = "shell", title = "Acme",
  shad_grid(kpi_one, kpi_two, kpi_three, min_width = "14rem")
)
```

## ⌘K navigation

`shad_command_palette()` is the "jump anywhere" pattern: a modal, searchable
list of everything the app can do, opened with ⌘K / Ctrl+K. Items come from
data — a named vector, or a named list of them for grouped sections:

```{r}
shad_command_palette("palette", items = list(
  "Go to"   = c(Dashboard = "dashboard", Reports = "reports"),
  "Actions" = list(
    list(value = "new", label = "New report", shortcut = "N",
         keywords = "create add")
  )
))
```

Drop `shad_command_trigger("palette")` in the page bar for people who do not
know the shortcut, and observe **`input$palette_event`** — not `input$palette`:

```{r}
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$palette_event, {
    switch(input$palette_event$value,
      dashboard = update_shad_tabs("nav", "dashboard"),
      reports   = update_shad_tabs("nav", "reports"),
      new       = shad_show_dialog(new_report_dialog())
    )
  })
}
```

`input$palette` holds the last value, but Shiny drops a repeat of the same
value — so choosing "Reports" twice would only fire once. `_event` carries
`value` plus a `nonce` and fires every time, which is what navigation needs.

`update_shad_command()` replaces the items from the server: recent documents,
search hits, commands gated on the signed-in user.

## The sidebar shell, by hand

`shad_page_sidebar()` is a thin wrapper over `shad_sidebar_layout()`. Use the
layout directly when the sidebar is one region of a larger page rather than the
page itself.

```{r}
sidebar <- shad_sidebar(
  header = tags$div(
    style = "display:flex;gap:0.5rem;align-items:center;padding:0.25rem",
    shad_icon("terminal"), tags$strong("Acme")
  ),
  shad_sidebar_group("Platform",
    shad_sidebar_item("home",   "Home",   icon = "circle", active = TRUE),
    shad_sidebar_item("inbox",  "Inbox",  icon = "mail", badge = "3"),
    shad_sidebar_item("search", "Search", icon = "search")
  ),
  shad_sidebar_group("Account",
    shad_sidebar_item("settings", "Settings", icon = "more-horizontal")
  ),
  footer = shad_muted(style = "padding:0.25rem", "v1.0.0")
)

ui <- page_shad(
  tags$div(style = "height:100vh",
    shad_sidebar_layout(
      "shell",
      sidebar = sidebar,
      main = tags$div(
        style = "padding:1.5rem",
        shad_sidebar_trigger(),        # the collapse toggle
        uiOutput("page")
      )
    )
  )
)
```

**Reading the sidebar.** The layout reports a list, not a scalar. Observe the
active item specifically:

```{r}
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # input$shell is list(collapsed=, mobileOpen=, active=)
  observeEvent(input$shell$active, {
    output$page <- renderUI(switch(input$shell$active,
      home = home_ui, inbox = inbox_ui, search = search_ui, settings = settings_ui
    ))
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
}
```

Toggle it from the server with `shad_sidebar_toggle("shell")` or
`update_shad_sidebar("shell", collapsed = TRUE)`.

## Resizable panes

For a two-pane workspace (list + detail, editor + preview), use
`shad_resizable()`:

```{r}
shad_resizable(
  "split",
  shad_resizable_panel(default_size = 35, list_ui),
  shad_resizable_handle(),
  shad_resizable_panel(default_size = 65, detail_ui)
)
```

## Scrollable regions

`shad_scroll_area(height = )` gives a fixed-height region a styled scrollbar —
useful for long lists inside a card or a chat transcript. For a growing
conversation that should pin to the bottom, reach for
`shad_message_scroller()` instead (see the
[chat gallery](../articles/gallery-chat.html)).

## Separators

`shad_separator()` draws a divider. Horizontal separators span the full width by
default, which overflows inside a flex row — give them `style = "flex:1"` when
using one as a rule between inline items (for example an "OR" divider).

```{r}
tags$div(style = "display:flex;align-items:center;gap:0.75rem",
  shad_separator(style = "flex:1"),
  shad_muted("OR"),
  shad_separator(style = "flex:1")
)
```
